subject: Live integration: parse instability causing increased errors & latency
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@clearwave.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production: sudden spike in streaming errors / p99 latency

Hi Marcus / Vanessa,

We're seeing a sharp degradation on our integration since last night (roughly 23:30 UTC on 2026-11-20). Our checkout stream to the Redwood streaming endpoint is returning intermittent 5xx errors and the p99 token latency has jumped from ~120ms to >1.2s in bursts. The error pattern looks like a parser/stream framing issue: our logs include repeated messages like "parse failed: unexpected header boundary" and a few 503s when the client retries.

Impact: about 7% of streaming requests fail end-to-end during peak traffic which is causing order processing delays. This is blocking our launch window for the holiday promotion.

I've attached a short pcap and a sample error payload from our side (capture_20261121.pcap, clearwave-error-sample.json). Ops are standing by for a call — can you confirm this is on your side and how quickly you can triage?

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Lead Integrations, ClearWave Labs
alex.johnson@clearwave.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: capture_20261121.pcap, clearwave-error-sample.json

Hi Alex — thank you for the heads up and the artifacts. Sorry you're hitting this.

Quick notes / immediate ask:
- We've received the pcap and sample; I'm looping in Vanessa (CS) and Rishi (infra) to prioritize.
- Can you confirm whether you're on the latest client SDK (v1.8.4)? If not, please include that version and whether you see the same behavior with a non-streaming (polling) endpoint.
- If you can reproduce quickly, please toggle debug = true in the client and attach the client logs (redwood-client-logs-20261121.tar.gz) — that helps us map the state machine transitions.

We'll triage now and aim to have an initial engineering response within 4 hours. If this is causing business disruption, we can also standby for an on-call bridge.

—I’ll follow up with a technical update shortly.

Subject: FW: Production: sudden spike in streaming errors / p99 latency

Team — escalating. Customer ClearWave Labs (high-revenue account, on Dedicated reserve DL-7832) is seeing ~7% failure rate retries and significant p99 spikes. They are live and the holiday campaign is time-sensitive.

Repro notes provided by customer:
- Client SDK: unsure (asking for confirmation).
- Failures are intermittent and correlate with brief TCP bursts; see attached pcap.
- Error text: "parse failed: unexpected header boundary" present in both client logs and server logs.

Please prioritize this as P0 for the next shift. If this looks like an SDK integration issue we should prepare a temporary mitigation (server-side coalescing or an explicit non-streaming fallback) and an exec-facing summary.

Link to ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/ticket/987654

Thanks — Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 14:00:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: FW: Production: sudden spike in streaming errors / p99 latency

Initial triage results (quick summary):
- Reproduced locally using ClearWave pcap + their sample emitter. Root cause appears to be the client SDK streaming parser state machine failing to reconcile HTTP-like header frames when TCP segmentation results in mid-header fragment deliveries. The parser drops the continuation frame which leaves an unterminated header state and triggers a parse error downstream on the Redwood runtime.
- The runtime logs we have show repeated "header-fragment-unexpected" traces followed by connection resets at ~50–200ms after the first fragment. That lines up with the customer's capture.

Immediate mitigations we can apply:
1) Server-side: enable header coalescing on the streaming ingress to reconstruct segmented header frames (config flag: ingress.coalesce_headers=true). This is a safe short-term mitigation we can flip without code changes; expect a rollback-friendly canary in < 4 hours.
2) Client-side: ask ClearWave to upgrade to SDK v1.8.5 (we have a patch that hardens header reassembly) — ETA for release and client-side rollout is ~24–48 hours depending on their release process.
3) Fallback: enforce non-streaming (long-poll) for their highest-risk routes while we canary the server fix.

I've opened INF-1209 and pushed the minimal header-reassembly patch into a canary branch. Patch note: guard the parser against state resets on partial header frames and delay connection reset until a full parse verdict is available. Logs attached (redwood-client-logs-20261121.tar.gz contains our repro run).

Next steps:
- Marcus / Vanessa: coordinate the customer for a short maintenance window to flip ingress.coalesce_headers in canary and validate.
- Sean: can you lead the canary rollout? We want telemetry on error-rate delta and p99 within first 100k tokens. I'll prepare dashboards.

Quoted sample from our runtime logs: 
"[2026-11-22T13:42:06Z] header-fragment-unexpected: conn=cbf7, offset=1024
[2026-11-22T13:42:06Z] parse-failure: conn=cbf7, reason=unterminated-header
[2026-11-22T13:42:06Z] conn-reset: conn=cbf7, cause=parser-failure
"

Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-client-logs-20261121.tar.gz

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@clearwave.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden spike in streaming errors / p99 latency

Alex — quick update and next steps from our side. Appreciate your patience while we investigated.

Summary:
- What happened: a parser edge case in handling segmented header frames from the client SDK led to unterminated header states on our streaming ingress and occasional connection resets. This manifests as intermittent parse errors and p99 latency spikes.
- Short-term mitigation (canary): we will enable ingress.coalesce_headers=true in a controlled canary this evening to reassemble segmented headers at the edge. Expected time to first telemetry: ~30 minutes after flip. Rollback plan in place.
- Client fix: we have a client SDK patch (v1.8.5) that hardens header reassembly; recommended for ClearWave once tested.
- Business accommodations: we understand the impact on your holiday launch. We'll provide a credit for the impacted minutes and prioritize your SDK patch review.

Proposed timeline:
- Tonight (within 4h): deploy canary with header coalescing, monitor for drop in errors.
- 24–48h: coordinate ClearWave SDK upgrade to v1.8.5; if they prefer we can back a short-lived proxy change to avoid requiring an immediate client change.
- 72h: full rollout if canary meets success criteria (error rate <0.5% and p99 within normal bounds).

Would you like us to schedule a 30-minute bridge now or wait until we have canary telemetry?

Again, apologies for the disruption — we'll stay on this with urgency.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Engineer, Redwood Inference
